proof:
By joint-measure-homothetic-domination-and-strata, each stratum is a complete base, every $\mu_z$ is absolutely continuous in its affine support, and the support Minkowski combinations are compatible at every anchored representation. On a fixed stratum, projecting those combinations to $V^\perp$ gives $b_z=\sum_i\theta_i b_{z_i}$. Each scalar coordinate of $b_z$ therefore preserves all anchored representations. Accepted facts ba0f3db1bf4f62c6 and e557f3071b96c191 give the canonical integer graph, its affine maps $\pi,B$, exact lattice completeness, and preservation of the parity count. In particular, an integer point of its hull is a lifted site, and projecting a lifted anchored representation gives precisely an original one.

We give the density and compatibility details. For $q>0$, the Fubini bound in the domination predecessor bounds each intrinsic density by $2^N\mu_z(S_z)/|S_z|_q$ almost everywhere. The boundary of the convex support is intrinsically Lebesgue-null. Work first with one measure $\mu_z$ in its intrinsic affine plane, and let $g_\varepsilon(x)$ be its mass in the open $\varepsilon$-ball divided by the intrinsic volume of that ball. On $\operatorname{relint}S_z$, the joint inequality with both bases equal gives concavity of $g_\varepsilon^{1/N}$. For the open balls this follows by approximating input masses with compact subsets and using containment of their weighted Minkowski sum in the open ball of the same radius. The functions are nonnegative and uniformly bounded by the density bound. On compact subsets of $\operatorname{relint}S_z$, concavity and the uniform bound imply local uniform Lipschitz bounds by extending each short secant a fixed positive distance within the interior on both sides. Thus along a sequence $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, compact exhaustion and Arzelà–Ascoli give a locally uniform concave limit $h$ of $g_\varepsilon^{1/N}$. By Fubini the measures with densities $g_\varepsilon$ converge weakly to $\mu_z$, since their integrals against a compactly supported continuous test function are the averages of that test over shrinking balls integrated against $\mu_z$. It follows that $g_z=h^N$ is the continuous density on the relative interior. A nonnegative concave $h$ vanishing at an interior point vanishes throughout the interior by taking a strict convex combination through that point, contradicting positive mass of interior balls. The density is therefore positive there, and continuity makes the representative unique.

Take $x_i\in\operatorname{relint}S_{z_i}$ for an anchored representation in the stratum and put $x=\sum_i\theta_i x_i$. The supports have parallel planes with common tangent $V$, so the sum of small relative balls about the $x_i$ contains a relative ball about $x$ in $S_z$. Thus $x$ is interior there. Apply the joint inequality to relative balls of radii $\varepsilon a_i$ about $x_i$, where $a_i>0$ and $\sum_i\theta_i a_i=1$. Their weighted sum is the relative ball of radius $\varepsilon$ about $x$. By continuity of the densities, dividing by the common volume factor to power $1/N$ and sending $\varepsilon$ to zero gives
$$
g_z(x)^{1/N}\ge\sum_i\theta_i g_{z_i}(x_i)^{1/N}a_i^{q/N}.
$$
Set $a_i=g_{z_i}(x_i)^{1/r}/\sum_l\theta_l g_{z_l}(x_l)^{1/r}$. Because $q+r=N$, the right side becomes $(\sum_i\theta_i g_{z_i}(x_i)^{1/r})^{r/N}$. Raising to $N/r$ gives cross-fiber concavity of the radius functions. Taking all bases equal gives concavity of $g_z^{1/r}$ in each interior. The density bound makes its upper-limit extension $\bar f_z$ finite and upper semicontinuous. For arbitrary support inputs choose interior sequences converging to the inputs with radius values tending to the corresponding upper limits. Upper semicontinuity at the output gives $\bar f_z(\sum_i\theta_i x_i)\ge\sum_i\theta_i\bar f_{z_i}(x_i)$ also on the boundary, and in particular makes each extension concave. If $q=0$, the same compatibility inequality follows by testing singleton atoms in the joint inequality.

The sets $K_z$ are compact and convex by upper semicontinuity and concavity of the radius, with nonempty interior by its positivity on the relative interior of each support. At an anchored representation the offset identity makes the weighted continuous coordinates align and the triangle inequality with radius compatibility gives $\sum_i\theta_i K_{z_i}\subseteq K_z$. By exact preservation of representations this holds on the canonical graph as well. The lattice completeness of the graph leaves no extra integer bases in the hull, and fiber compatibility leaves no extra points in its fibers. The hull has full dimension in the product of its base affine span and $V\times\mathbb R^r$ since the individual fibers have dimension $N$ and the bases span their affine hull. Passing to a basis of the saturated affine lattice changes only the base coordinates.

By Fubini the hidden ball contributes volume $\bar f_z^r=g_z$ almost everywhere in the intrinsic support, whose boundary has zero mass. At $q=0$ the ball volume is $\mu_z(S_z)$. The affine projection in the statement therefore preserves the entire stratum measure. A physical closed halfspace containing the projected mark pulls back to a closed halfspace containing the lifted mark or to the whole space. This proves the depth transfer for every physical orientation.

In the non-hollow case nonhollow-joint-slice-affine-support-graph gives one stratum and one affine perpendicular offset on the original base. Apply the same fiber compatibility and projection argument there, using the lattice completeness of $P$.

For the conditional conclusion, apply the assumed occupied-parity theorem to each canonical lifted body. The projections give physical marks of stratum depth at least $\Gamma_N W_c/k_c$ for stratum mass $W_c$. The largest $W_c/k_c$ is at least $\sum_c W_c/\sum_c k_c=W/k(P)$ by parity disjointness. The full measure can only increase every cap mass at that chosen mark. The required bound is in terms of $k_c$ because the rank of the canonical integer graph can increase.

statement:
Let $n\ge0$, $N\ge1$, and let $\mu_z$ be nonzero finite positive Borel measures of compact support $S_z\subset\mathbb R^D$ indexed by a finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$. Suppose every positive-weight combination $z=\sum_i\theta_i z_i\in\mathbb Z^n$, with $z_i\in P$ and $\sum_i\theta_i=1$, has $z\in P$ and satisfies $\mu_z(\sum_i\theta_i E_i)^{1/N}\ge\sum_i\theta_i\mu_{z_i}(E_i)^{1/N}$ for compact positive-mass $E_i$. Let $P_c$ be any stratum of equal support affine dimension $q<N$ and common tangent space $V$, and let $b_z\in V^\perp$ be the perpendicular offset of $\operatorname{aff}(S_z)$.

There is a canonical integer graph placement $\Psi(P_c)$ in its saturated affine lattice, preserving precisely the anchored representations and the number $k_c$ of original occupied parities. Its affine span carries affine maps $\pi,B$ with $\pi(\Psi(z))=z$ and $B(\Psi(z))=b_z$. Put $r=N-q$. For $q>0$ let $g_z$ be the continuous positive intrinsic density on $\operatorname{relint} S_z$, and let $\bar f_z$ be the finite upper-limit extension of $g_z^{1/r}$ to $S_z$. For $q=0$ use the value $\bar f_z=\mu_z(S_z)^{1/N}$ on the single point. Let $\omega_r$ be the volume of the unit ball in $\mathbb R^r$. The sets
$$
K_z=\{(v,u)\in V\times\mathbb R^r:b_z+v\in S_z,\quad
\lVert u\rVert\le\bar f_z(b_z+v)/\omega_r^{1/r}\}
$$
are full $N$-dimensional convex bodies. The hull of the fibers $K_z$ placed over $\Psi(z)$ has exactly those integer fibers in its saturated affine lattice. Its summed fiber $N$-volume pushes forward by $(t,v,u)\mapsto(\pi(t),B(t)+v)$ to the entire physical stratum law $\sum_{z\in P_c}\delta_z\otimes\mu_z$. Every lifted mixed point projects to an actual support point whose raw depth for the represented measure is at least the raw depth of that point for lifted mixed volume.

If the entire positive base has a relative-interior integer point and its support ranks are less than $N$, the same bodies give the exact lift over the original bases in their own saturated affine lattice, using an affine offset map on the original base. If all strata have ranks less than $N$ and ordinary mixed convex bodies in continuous dimension $N$ and every integer rank have a point of raw depth at least $\Gamma_N$ times mass divided by their occupied positive-base parity count, where $\Gamma_N=(N/(N+1))^N$, then the whole physical law has an actual support point of raw depth at least $\Gamma_N$ times its mass divided by $k(P)$.
title: Exact convex lifts for rank-deficient joint slice laws on canonical integer graphs
